Final categorization: OK  
(Justification: The paper presents a national-scale spatial analysis of Australian agricultural land use change to 2050 using the LUTO model, which simulates future land use transitions across ~85 million ha of Australia’s intensively managed agricultural lands—an area covering major production zones from Queensland to Western Australia. The primary research objective is to explore plausible future trajectories of land use and agricultural production under multiple global outlooks (four scenarios), productivity assumptions (three levels), adoption rates (three hurdle rates), and capacity constraints (two settings), resulting in 72 unique quantitative scenario combinations. The modeling is spatially explicit at ~1.1 km resolution, includes mapped outputs of land use change (e.g., Figs. 4, 5, S1–S8), and quantifies changes in land use area, production, output rates, and economic value over time. Although focused on agricultural and new non-food land uses (e.g., carbon plantings, biofuels), it meets all core inclusion criteria: national-scale spatial implementation, primary focus on LULC prediction, ≥2 future scenarios with quantitative comparison, spatial modeling with quantitative metrics (e.g., hectares converted, % change in area), and mapped projections. It does not fall under exclusion criteria—it is not global-only, not local/regional only, includes explicit LULC change analysis beyond carbon/bioenergy alone, and is not methodological or qualitative.)
